_about: Volunteer station cards for the Get Set Go dashboard (admin portal → Get Set Go Sessions).

Every series gets a card per station per week. Cards listed here are hand-condensed; every other card is built automatically from the Notion Rotations board by scripts/build_sessions.mjs and marked for review.

Source precedence: the current Get Set Go Rotations board → the current 2026–27 weekly lessons → older drafts (reference only). Nothing here may contradict the Rotations board; where the board is silent, the card says so in `review` instead of inventing content.
Committee edits made in the portal are saved to the Notion database 'Get Set Go — Station Cards' as overrides and never touch this file or the Rotations board.
An image is only used once its file exists in public/getsetgo/stations/ — the build skips (and lists) any that are missing, so the card shows a placeholder instead of a broken image.

eventSafety.High jump: High jump mat with a low breakaway elastic — never a high jump pole or rigid bar. Feet-first landings only — no back landings, no flop.
eventSafety.Hurdles: Foam hurdles only — the kind that fall over when clipped. Never rigid hurdles.

1.coachNote: First two weeks: learn the names of the four or five children at each station and use them out loud. Walk the boundary cones on night one.
conflicts: Notion's Week 01 lesson once said Long jump / Jump and Freeze; the Rotations board says High jump / Scissor Basics. The seniors do long jump on 15 Oct, so High jump is right — check the Week 01 page in Notion matches.
An older draft listed Station 4 as sprint starts and Station 3 as Farmyard. Ignored — the Rotations board wins.
Circus Throws: the board's kit is 8 hula hoops and soft toys, but the Discovery stage rolls beanbags. Bring beanbags if you use that stage.
Scissor Basics: the board's equipment list leaves out the high jump mat, but its safety rule requires it. The card lists the mat as required.
The Scissor Basics illustration shows a rigid bar and a child landing on grass. The card carries an 'illustration only' caption — a replacement image showing an elastic and the mat would be better.

A.name: Traffic Lights
A.setup: Mark a wide playing space with cones. Spread children out and check the boundaries together.
steps: GREEN = jog; ORANGE = walk; RED = freeze.
Add CROSSING (sideways) and ROUNDABOUT (turn on the spot).
Change the call every 10–15 seconds; use children's names.
Nobody is out. If someone moves on red, do one star jump and carry on.
A.younger: Use GREEN and RED only; walk with a helper.
A.older: Add direction changes and turning on command.
A.watch: Eyes up — children watching the floor instead of the space. Avoid collisions.
A.safety: Keep children inside the cone boundary. No elimination.
A.discovery: Walk and jog through a roomy cone-marked space; invent your own way of stopping.
A.developing: GREEN jog, ORANGE walk, RED freeze. Practise looking up and pumping arms while moving.
A.consolidating: A child caller adds CROSSING or ROUNDABOUT. Everyone joins every round.
A.observation: Are eyes looking ahead, and are children avoiding collisions?
A.alternative: Fast Cars — run laps around the area; on the call, change gear: walk, jog, run, sprint.
sources: Club Series 1 package (condensed from the Rotations board)

B.name: Octopus
B.setup: Mark two safe lines at either end of the space with cones. One walking octopus waits in the middle.
steps: Children move from one safe line to the other on GO.
The octopus walks and gently tags; tagged children become seaweed.
Seaweed stand still, arms waving, and can reach to tag runners.
Keep rounds short — change the octopus and restart often.
B.younger: Walking octopus and a short crossing; give younger children a head start.
B.older: Weave around two safe taggers when ready.
B.watch: Head-up dodging without colliding.
B.safety: Walking taggers and gentle touches only. No elimination — everyone plays every round.
B.discovery: Explore crossing the space without a tagger, noticing open gaps.
B.developing: One walking octopus tags runners gently; touched children become stationary seaweed.
B.consolidating: Vary the route, plan a gap around the seaweed and encourage head-up dodges; reset quickly.
B.observation: Can the child change direction without crashing into others?
B.alternative: Fast Cars — run laps around the area; on the call, change gear: walk, jog, run, sprint.
sources: Rotations board: Week B progression and observation

A.name: Circus Throws
A.setup: Place hoops flat on the ground at close, middle and far distances. Keep the throwing lanes clear.
steps: Choose a hoop and stand at the throwing line.
Throw a soft toy underarm towards your hoop.
Take three turns, then try a different distance.
Cheer every attempt. Move a hoop closer when needed.
A.younger: Use a close, large hoop; roll or two-handed push first.
A.older: Try a smaller target or a hoop further away.
A.watch: Same foot forward as the throwing arm — step with the OPPOSITE foot.
A.safety: Throw one way only. Children collect toys on the coach's signal.
A.discovery: Roll a beanbag towards a large floor hoop and notice where it goes. (Bring beanbags if you use this stage.)
A.developing: Swing the throwing arm back and forward; step with the opposite foot and gently release into a nearby hoop.
A.consolidating: Try hoops at two distances; choose a target and explain how much force you needed.
A.observation: Are feet opposite the throwing arm?
A.alternative: Toy Basketball — an adult holds a hoop up as the basket; throw the toy in, then swap. Rotate quickly.
sources: Club Series 1 package (condensed from the Rotations board)

B.name: Bin It
B.setup: Set targets at close, middle and far distances. Keep the throwing lanes clear.
steps: Set buckets and hoops at safe, close and further distances.
Children choose a target and make several underarm attempts.
Count each child's own successful throws out loud.
Try to beat their own count — bring targets closer as needed.
B.younger: Large, low bucket and a close line.
B.older: Change the target height and distance.
B.watch: Adjusting force to the target rather than just throwing harder.
B.safety: Throw one way only. Children collect toys on the coach's signal.
B.discovery: Experiment with low, medium and high target positions using soft objects.
B.developing: Single-hand underarm toss with an opposite step; practise release height and follow-through.
B.consolidating: Choose a close, medium or far bucket; try the same target twice and notice progress.
B.observation: Does the child adjust force rather than simply throwing harder?
B.alternative: Toy Basketball — an adult holds a hoop up as the basket; throw the toy in, then swap. Rotate quickly.
B.review: Steps are a draft from the older Series 1 lesson — the Rotations board only has Bin It's name, cues and progression. Bin It uses buckets, which aren't on the station equipment list: confirm we have them or use hoops.
sources: Rotations board: Week B progression and observation

A.name: Animal Trail
A.setup: Arrange the six activities around a spacious one-way loop. Start children at different activities so nobody queues.
steps: Bear crawl — hands and feet, bottom up, cone A to B.
Frog jumps — jump over 3 flat markers; land softly on two feet.
Balance walk — along ground-level balance blocks, arms out.
Hurdle steps — carefully step over 3 low foam hurdles.
Flamingo balance — stand on each leg for 3 slow counts.
Crab walk — hands behind, bottom up, back to the start.
A.younger: Wide, low routes, supported balancing and fewer obstacles.
A.older: More controlled arms-out balance; longer safe holds.
A.watch: Queues, fatigue, collisions and unstable equipment.
A.safety: No racing. Floor-level blocks that can't slide; soft, low hurdles only.
A.discovery: Let children test each movement slowly and choose a comfortable way to do it; model eyes-forward, arms-out balance.
A.developing: Focus on one technique: stable feet, soft bent-knee landings or steady balance. Give short feedback.
A.consolidating: Turn it into a story mission while staying in control; children may choose a different safe route.
A.observation: Queues, fatigue, collisions and unstable or unsecured equipment.
sources: Club Series 1 package (condensed from the Rotations board course)

B.name: Animal Trail
B.setup: Same one-way loop as Week A. Start children at different activities so nobody queues.
steps: Bear crawl — hands and feet, bottom up, cone A to B.
Frog jumps — jump over 3 flat markers; land softly on two feet.
Balance walk — pause on the balance blocks for 3 counts, arms out.
Hurdle steps — carefully step over 3 low foam hurdles.
Flamingo balance — 3 slow counts; add a supported same-foot hop if ready.
Crab walk — hands behind, bottom up, back to the start.
B.younger: Repeat Week A's simpler route: wide, low paths and supported balancing.
B.older: Longer, still-controlled balance holds — never higher equipment.
B.watch: Queues, fatigue and unstable equipment.
B.safety: No racing. Floor-level blocks that can't slide; soft, low hurdles only.
B.discovery: Let children test each movement slowly and choose a comfortable way to do it.
B.developing: Add a supported same-foot hop after the flamingo if ready; pause on the balance blocks for 3 counts.
B.consolidating: Turn it into a story mission while staying in control; offer Week A's simpler route as an option.
B.observation: Queues, fatigue, collisions and unstable or unsecured equipment.

A.name: Scissor Basics
A.setup: Stretch a low breakaway elastic (never rope) between two cones at ankle-to-knee height, in front of the high jump mat. Mark a short diagonal approach with flat markers.
steps: Walk beside the low elastic and step one leg over.
Approach diagonally at walking pace.
Scissor the lead leg over, then follow with the other.
Land on your FEET with soft knees; repeat with control.
A.younger: Walk through a very low elastic; give support if needed.
A.older: Add a short diagonal run-up only with full control.
A.watch: Any attempt to land backwards or flop — stop immediately and reset.
A.safety: HIGH JUMP MAT REQUIRED. Breakaway elastic only — never a pole or rigid bar. Feet-first landings only.
A.discovery: Walk beside a very low elastic and explore stepping over with one foot, then the other.
A.developing: Approach diagonally at walking pace; scissor the lead leg over the low elastic, trail leg follows, land on feet.
A.consolidating: Choose a comfortable low elastic height; repeat with a smoother rhythm and land in control.
A.observation: No back landings or flop; breakaway elastic only.
A.alternative: Elastic Step-Over — walk in, step over the low elastic one leg then the other, walk out the far side.
sources: Club Series 1 package (condensed from the Rotations board)

B.name: Scissor Rhythm
B.setup: Same as Week A: a low breakaway elastic between two cones in front of the high jump mat, with a short diagonal approach.
steps: Start with a very low breakaway elastic and a clear mat.
Walk in diagonally; scissor one leg, then the other.
Make the approach and two-leg movement smoother.
Land feet-first with control; keep the elastic low.
B.younger: Slow walk-through of a very low elastic.
B.older: A slightly longer run-in, only while fully controlled — the elastic stays low.
B.watch: A faster approach that upsets balance, or any backwards landing.
B.safety: HIGH JUMP MAT REQUIRED. Breakaway elastic only — never a pole or rigid bar. Feet-first landings only.
B.discovery: Practise stepping over a low elastic and choose the leading foot.
B.developing: Approach with a few light steps; lead one leg and then the second across in a scissor action.
B.consolidating: Add arm drive and a more continuous approach while keeping feet-first landings.
B.observation: Is a faster approach upsetting balance?
B.alternative: Elastic Step-Over — walk in, step over the low elastic one leg then the other, walk out the far side.
B.review: Steps are a draft built from the board's name, cues and progression — the Rotations board has no full Week B how-to for Scissor Rhythm.
sources: Rotations board: Week B progression and observation

2.coachNote: Foam hurdles only — the kind that fall over when clipped. Never rigid hurdles at this age.

A.name: Jumping Beans
A.setup: Open space, everyone spread out.
steps: Call out a bean — the children do the action.
Jelly bean: wobble. Runner bean: run on the spot. String bean: stretch tall.
Baked bean: curl up small. Jumping bean: two-foot jumps. Frozen bean: freeze.
Add a new bean each week — let a child invent one.
A.younger: Small feet-together hops on the spot.
A.older: Reach up to a ribbon held overhead — never a high barrier.
A.watch: No arm swing — cue 'swing your arms up'.
A.discovery: Explore becoming a different bean: jelly bean wobble, string bean stretch, runner bean.
A.developing: On JUMPING BEAN, bend knees, swing arms and jump tall; on FROZEN BEAN, land and freeze.
A.consolidating: A child invents a bean and leads everyone. Compare a soft landing with a stiff landing.
A.observation: Can children land softly while staying in control?
A.alternative: Jump and Reach — jump up to touch a target held just above head height.

B.name: Beanbag Hop
B.setup: Open space with flat markers. Put beanbags on close markers.
steps: Stand on one foot, then the other — find your balance.
Tiny same-foot hops beside a line.
Hop on the SAME foot into a marked spot, pause, then swap feet.
Hop to collect a beanbag from a close marker, then walk back to rest.
B.younger: One supported hop, then rest — walking is fine.
B.older: Two or three connected same-foot hops, then change legs.
B.watch: Mixing up one-foot hops with two-foot jumps. No arm swing — cue 'swing your arms up'.
B.discovery: Explore standing on each foot, then a tiny same-foot hop beside a line.
B.developing: Hop on the SAME foot into a marked spot, pause, then swap feet; arms help balance.
B.consolidating: Collect a beanbag from a close marker using same-foot hops, then walk back to rest.
B.observation: Do children confuse single-leg hopping with two-foot jumping?
B.alternative: Jump and Reach — jump up to touch a target held just above head height.
B.review: The board's equipment says 'None', but its Week B progression uses beanbags and markers, so they're listed here. Set-up and steps come from the progression — check before sharing.
sources: Rotations board: S2 · R1 Week B progression (condensed)

A.name: Clever Catchers — floaters
A.setup: Partners about 2 m apart, or a child with an adult.
steps: Scarves first for the youngest — they float and can actually be caught.
Roll the ball, then bounce and catch.
Throw and catch with a bounce, then throw and catch in the air.
Only move up when the child is catching most of them.
A.younger: Scarf, balloon or rolled ball.
A.older: Move one step before catching a soft ball.
A.watch: Closing eyes as the ball arrives — use a bigger, softer, slower ball.
A.discovery: Watch a floating scarf travel through the air and bring hands towards it.
A.developing: An adult drops scarves and large soft balls into ready hands; children move their feet to line up.
A.consolidating: A partner tosses a soft ball with a bounce; the child tracks it, cups and draws the ball towards the body.
A.observation: Do eyes follow the object all the way in?
A.alternative: Scarf Pop — toss a scarf high, clap once, then catch it.

B.name: Clever Catchers — moving
B.setup: Partners about 2 m apart, or a child with an adult, with clear space to move into.
steps: Catch easy, slow underhand throws from a helper — hands open.
Catch after one bounce while moving feet sideways or forwards.
Pass and catch with a partner — one bounce first, then in the air if confident.
Change the throwing angle.
B.younger: Gentle adult throw from 1 m; catch against the body.
B.older: Catch while moving into clear, safe space.
B.watch: Closing eyes as the ball arrives — use a bigger, softer, slower ball.
B.discovery: Catch easy, slow underhand throws from a helper, hands open.
B.developing: Catch a ball after one bounce while moving feet sideways or forwards.
B.consolidating: Pass and catch with a partner, first one bounce then in the air if confident; change the throwing angle.
B.observation: Are hands adjusted for ball size and impact?
B.alternative: Scarf Pop — toss a scarf high, clap once, then catch it.
sources: Rotations board: S2 · R2 Week B progression (condensed)

A.name: Jungle Jaunt
A.setup: Set the six activities around a one-way loop. Start children at different activities so nobody queues.
steps: Snake slither — on your tummy from A to B; arms and legs push you along.
Frog jumps — hoop to hoop (lily pads); two-foot take-off and landing.
Bear crawl — over 2 low boxes; hands on the box, walk over on all fours.
Balance blocks — arms out, one foot in front of the other.
Log roll — from A to B; lie down, arms over your head, roll like a log.
Flamingo balance — one foot for a slow count of 3; arms out, look at one spot.
A.younger: Low, wide pathways, supported balancing and fewer obstacles.
A.older: Controlled arms-out balance and longer challenges — never raise the equipment.
A.watch: Landing on straight legs — demonstrate the ninja landing yourself.
A.safety: Watch for queues, fatigue, collisions and unstable or unsecured equipment.
A.discovery: Let children test each movement slowly and choose a comfortable way to do it; model eyes-forward, arms-out balance.
A.developing: Focus on one technique: stable feet, soft bent-knee landings or steady balance. Give short feedback.
A.consolidating: Turn it into a story mission while staying in control; children may choose a different safe route.
A.observation: Queues, fatigue, collisions and unstable or unsecured equipment.
A.review: The Rotations board has no cues or set-up for Jungle Jaunt. The cues come from its Developing text and the set-up from Animal Trail's loop — check both.

A.name: Step and Run — hurdles
A.setup: A line of foam hurdles — the kind that collapse if clipped — at shin height, spaced close together.
steps: Run towards the hurdles.
Step over each one without stopping.
Run on through the finish cone.
If they stop, move the hurdles closer together.
A.younger: Very low foam markers; walk.
A.older: Jog in a continuous rhythm over knock-over hurdles.
A.watch: Stopping before each hurdle — space them closer together.
A.safety: Foam hurdles only — never rigid hurdles. Never race into a fallen hurdle.
A.discovery: Walk over widely spaced flat markers, lifting knees and looking ahead.
A.developing: Step over three foam hurdles in rhythm and run on to finish.
A.consolidating: Try a connected approach and clearance without stopping; never race into a fallen hurdle.
A.observation: Rushed foot contact or rigid hurdles: stop and simplify.
A.alternative: Hurdle Hop — hop over each low foam hurdle on two feet, one hop per hurdle.

B.name: Hurdle Rhythm
B.setup: A line of foam hurdles — the kind that collapse if clipped — at shin height, evenly spaced.
steps: Two-foot jump, then step over one low obstacle.
Jog and step over 3 soft hurdles with even spacing — eyes ahead.
Run through 4 low hurdles smoothly.
Find a rhythm — not the fastest time.
B.younger: Flat markers instead of hurdles.
B.older: Adjust the spacing to practise more continuous strides.
B.watch: Stopping before each hurdle — space them closer together.
B.safety: Foam hurdles only — never rigid hurdles. Never race into a fallen hurdle.
B.discovery: Explore a two-foot jump and stepping over one low obstacle.
B.developing: Jog and step over 3 soft hurdles with consistent spacing; eyes ahead.
B.consolidating: Run through 4 low hurdles smoothly, finding a rhythm rather than the fastest time.
B.observation: Change the spacing to suit the child, not the other way round.
B.alternative: Hurdle Hop — hop over each low foam hurdle on two feet, one hop per hurdle.
sources: Rotations board: S2 · R4 Week B progression (condensed)

A.name: Circle Dodge Ball
A.setup: A coned area with clear safety boundaries and a line down the middle (or a marked circle). Soft dodgeballs ready.
steps: Roll or gently throw the soft balls underarm — below the knees only.
Dodgers bend, plant a foot and move away from the rolling ball.
Tagged? Run to the sideline, do five star jumps and rejoin.
Swap rollers and dodgers often — nobody is out for long.
A.younger: Roll instead of dodge if needed; use a wider circle.
A.older: Quick changes of direction around two slow rollers.
A.watch: Throwing too hard — cue 'below the knees, gentle'.
A.safety: Soft balls only, rolled or thrown underarm below the knees — no head-height throws. No elimination: tagged players rejoin straight after their star jumps.
A.discovery: Explore stepping left and right in response to calls while others hold the soft balls.
A.developing: Bend knees, plant the outside foot and move around a rolling ball; no throws above the knees.
A.consolidating: In a marked circle, dodge gently rolled soft balls and return to the ready position; switch roles.
A.observation: Keep balls rolling slowly, with no head-height launches.
A.alternative: Dodgeball Roll — roll a ball along the ground to touch another player's feet; swap roles after a touch.

B.name: Dragon's Tail
equipment: Soft tails for the back child
B.setup: Spacious coned play zone with clear safety boundaries.
steps: Follow the leader, changing direction at a walking pace.
Make short lines of 3–4; the back child wears a soft tail.
One gentle tagger tries to take the tail; the line moves together to protect it.
Try a feint and a safe turn. Rotate every minute so everyone leads.
B.younger: Walk, with a helper leading a short line.

steps: Hold the wide foam bat with two hands together, stand side on and watch the ball on the tee.
Step and swing level through the ball, then follow through.
Choose a target arc, strike from the tee and say where the ball travelled.
After your hit, run to your cone and back. The run path stays outside the striking lanes.

equipment: 20 cones (lane markers and wide target gates)

steps: Explore the angle of the bat against the large, still ball on the tee.
Step forward, turn your hips and make a controlled two-hand level swing.
Strike off the tee towards the wide target gate.
Carefully try changing how hard you swing. Adults retrieve on the coach's signal.

B.older: A gently rolled ball, only with a skilled feeder and a clear area.

B.discovery: Explore the angle of the bat against a large, still ball on the tee.
B.developing: Rotate the hips, step forward and make a controlled two-hand horizontal swing.
B.consolidating: Strike off the tee towards a wide target gate; change the swing force carefully.

A.name: Frosty's Winter Trail
A.setup: Six small stations around a spacious one-way loop, 1–2 children per station. Start groups at different stations so nobody queues. Week A focus: tell children the snow-mound leaps and bunny jumps are two-foot jumps, not hopping.
steps: Penguin waddle — heels together, short shuffling steps from A to B.
Ice skate — side-step beside the low balance blocks, like skating on ice; eyes up.
Snow mounds — two-foot jumps over 3 low foam hurdles; bend your knees and land quietly.
Snowflake balance — stand on either foot, arms out wide, look at one spot and count to 3.
Bear crawl — on all fours through the snow tunnel; stay between the two cone lines.
Bunny jumps — two feet together, small jumps to the finish.
A.younger: Low, wide pathways, supported balancing and fewer obstacles if needed.
A.older: Controlled arms-out balance and longer (but still manageable) challenges. Never raise the equipment.
A.watch: Jumping off one foot. Cue 'two feet to land'.
A.safety: Not a race. Soft foam hurdles that collapse if clipped; never rigid hurdles. Balance blocks stay on the ground; no raised or unsecured obstacles. Snow mounds and bunny jumps are two-foot jumps: take off and land on two feet.
A.discovery: First lap: let children test each movement slowly and choose a comfortable way to do it; model eyes-forward, arms-out balance.
A.developing: Second lap: focus on one technique (stable feet, a soft bent-knee landing or steady balance) and give short feedback.
A.consolidating: Last lap: turn it into an imagined story mission while staying in control; children may choose a different safe route.
A.observation: Queues, fatigue, collisions and unstable or unsecured equipment.

A.name: Jump and Freeze — revisit
equipment: 30 cones (start line, waiting spaces, personal markers)
A.setup: A start line and an age-appropriate runway leading to the long jump mat or sandpit. Mark waiting spaces, and have a cone ready for each child's personal marker.
steps: Next to the line, explore a safe landing and an arm swing.
Swing your arms, push off two feet and reach forwards.
Land on two feet in the mat or pit with bent knees, then freeze!
Place your own cone where you landed.
Use the same start and the same arm swing to try to beat your OWN cone. Nobody compares with anybody else.
A.younger: A standing jump of 20–40 cm is success.
A.older: A controlled short approach for ready six-year-olds, still with a two-foot take-off and landing.
A.watch: Children comparing themselves with each other. Redirect: 'beat your own cone'.
A.safety: Long jump = two-foot take-off and two-foot landing into the mat or pit; no hopping here. Each child beats their OWN marker; never compare children. Wait in the marked waiting spaces.
A.discovery: Explore a safe landing and an arm swing next to the line.
A.developing: Two-foot push, reach forwards, and a quiet two-foot bent-knee landing.
A.consolidating: Place a personal marker and practise a consistent arm swing from the same start.
A.observation: Landing with the hands behind the hips.
A.alternative: Frog Jump Freeze: jump forward with two feet, then freeze the landing in a bent-knee shape.

equipment: 30 cones (personal take-off lines, waiting spaces, markers)

steps: Rehearse the take-off at your own personal line and land stable on two feet.
Take 2–3 approach steps, then plant and push off two feet.
Keep the landing balanced: two feet, knees bent, into the mat or pit.
Choose a standing jump or a short-run jump.
Compare only with your own earlier jumps, and keep every attempt safe and controlled.

B.older: A short run-up, only with proper space.

B.consolidating: Choose a standing jump or a short-run jump and compare your own safe, controlled attempts.
B.observation: Don't sacrifice a stable two-foot landing for distance.
B.alternative: Frog Jump Freeze: jump forward with two feet, then freeze the landing in a bent-knee shape.

A.name: Cat & Mouse
A.setup: A wide, coned play zone with clear safety boundaries. Put out one or two mouse holes (hoops or a square of cones) as safe zones. Add extra mouse holes for younger groups.
steps: Mice explore easy running between the mouse holes. No cat yet.
Add one walking cat who gently tags the mice.
A mouse is safe in a mouse hole for a slow count of five, then must run again.
Tagged? You become a cat too, but keep the number of cats small.
Swap the cats often so everyone gets a turn chasing. Nobody is out.
Last round: change the spaces and move around a gentle tagger, head up, with quiet stops.

A.older: Quicker but controlled routes between the holes.

Step forward with one foot, push both arms straight towards the ready target and follow through.

B.name: Team Dodge Challenge
B.setup: A spacious coned play zone with clear safety boundaries. Spread marker cones around it for the direction changes.
steps: Explore 2–3 changes of direction around the marker cones.
In small groups, play gentle tag: bend, plant your outside foot and push towards a gap.
Each child tells the group their dodge plan, then tries it in the tag game.
Swap roles often so everyone dodges and everyone tags. Nobody is out.
The group counts its safe turns together. There are no individual winners.
B.younger: Walk, in a larger safe area.
B.older: Add a shoulder feint and quick changes of direction.
B.watch: Collisions while changing direction. Keep the groups small and the area wide.
B.safety: Gentle tags only, and no elimination: swap roles so everyone dodges and everyone tags. No collisions while changing direction. Stay inside the coned boundaries.
B.discovery: Explore 2–3 direction changes around marker cones.
B.developing: Play gentle tag in small groups: bend, plant the outside foot, push towards a gap.
B.consolidating: Each child explains a dodge strategy, uses it in tag and swaps roles; cooperative scoring for safe turns.
B.observation: No collisions while changing direction.
B.alternative: Farmers and Chickens: chickens run the whole width, and tagged chickens become farmers and join the chase.
B.review: The board's set-up and how-to are written for Tigers and Cheetahs (Week A), so these Week B steps come from the board's Week B progression and the Week 18 lesson. Neither source explains how the 'cooperative scoring for safe turns' works, so the card has the group count its safe turns together. Confirm.
sources: Rotations board: S9 · R1 Week B progression

A.name: Target Toys — underarm recap
A.setup: A row of hula hoops on the ground at three distances (close, middle and far), with one clear throwing lane per 2–3 children. Everyone throws the same way.
steps: Roll or toss a beanbag underarm into the close hoop.
Step with the OPPOSITE foot and swing your arm smoothly, like a pendulum. Let go towards the target.
Choose which hoop to aim at: close, middle or far. Everyone gets three throws, and we cheer every attempt.
Repeat the target challenge. Is your throw more controlled than last time?
Collect only on the coach's signal. Move the close hoop closer for anyone who is struggling.
A.younger: A large floor hoop 1 m away.
A.older: Targets at different heights and distances.
A.watch: Throwing with the same foot forward as the throwing arm. Chalk a footprint.
A.safety: Soft toys and beanbags only, and no hard throws towards people. Everyone throws the same way down their own lane. Collect only on the coach's signal, never across another lane. Throwing lanes stay clear of running paths.
A.discovery: Roll and toss beanbags underarm to a close target.
A.developing: Opposite step, smooth pendulum arm and accurate release; choose a closer or farther target.
A.consolidating: Repeat the target accuracy challenge; report personal improvement in control.
A.observation: Does the release adjust to the target distance?
A.alternative: Toy Basketball: one person holds a hoop up as the basket. The front of the line throws a soft toy in, then swaps with the holder.
A.review: The beanbags come from the Week 17 lesson (Discover and the equipment checklist). The board lists only hoops and soft toys. Confirm.

B.name: Force Back — overarm recap
B.skill: Overarm throwing · near and far targets
equipment: 8 hula hoops (near and far target zones)
B.setup: One clear throwing lane per 2–3 children, all throwing the same way. Each lane has a wide near zone and a farther marked zone. Soft equipment only.
steps: Stand side on. Try an underarm throw, then an overarm throw, and feel the difference.
Overarm: your pointing hand aims at the target and your other hand goes back.
Step with the opposite foot and follow through with your throwing arm.
Choose the best throw for the near or far zone and make 3 controlled throws. Tell the coach why you chose it.
Everyone throws the same way. Collect only on the coach's signal.
B.younger: Beanbags into a wide near zone.
B.older: Shift your body weight and aim at the farther marked zone.
B.watch: Everyone throwing the same way and waiting for the signal to collect. Also, the same foot stepping as the throwing arm: chalk a footprint.
B.safety: Beanbags and soft toys only, and no hard throws towards people. All throws go one way down your own lane into a clear zone. Collect only on the coach's signal, never across another lane. Throwing lanes stay clear of running paths.
B.discovery: Compare underarm and overarm motion safely while standing side on.
B.developing: Overarm: the pointing hand aims, the other hand goes back, the opposite foot steps and the arm follows through.
B.consolidating: Choose a suitable throw for a near or far target; make 3 controlled throws and explain the choice.
B.observation: Throws go in the same direction; retrieve on the signal.
B.alternative: Toy Basketball: one person holds a hoop up as the basket. The front of the line throws a soft toy in, then swaps with the holder.
B.review: The board's set-up, how-to and equipment are written for Target Toys (Week A). These Week B steps come from the board's Week B progression and the Week 18 lesson. Those sources describe near and far target throws, not the Series 3 Force Back partner game where you push your partner back, so the card doesn't use partners. The beanbags come from the lesson checklist and the 3–4 option. The board lists no cones for this station, so the hoops mark the near and far zones. Confirm.
sources: Rotations board: S9 · R2 Week B progression

A.name: Challenge Trail
equipment: 10 cones (A–B markers and the one-way loop)
4 soft foam hurdles (they fall over if clipped)
A.setup: Six small stations around a spacious one-way loop, 1–2 children per station. Groups start at different stations so nobody queues. Week A: the one-foot balance is supportive and optional, and five counts can become two.
steps: Bear crawl — all fours from A to B at a steady personal pace. No timing, no racing.
Frog jumps — TWO-foot jumps over the 4 flat markers; bend your knees to land.
Balance walk — the whole length of the low balance blocks: arms out, heel-to-toe, slow. You can also walk alongside them.
One-foot balance — look at one spot, arms out, and hold for a slow count of 5 on each foot. Holding a hand is fine.
Hurdle step-overs — lift your knees over the 4 soft foam hurdles; head up, keep moving.
Crab walk — backwards to the finish at a comfortable pace: hands behind, bottom up.
A.younger: Low, wide pathways, supported balancing and fewer obstacles if needed. The five-count balance can become two.
A.older: Controlled arms-out balance and longer (but still manageable) challenges. Never raise the equipment.
A.watch: Frustration when they step off the blocks. Reassure them: 'stepping off is part of learning'. Also watch for queues, fatigue and collisions.
A.safety: Not a race: no timing and no speed contests. Use soft foam hurdles that fall over if clipped, never rigid hurdles. Balance blocks stay on the ground, with no raised or unsecured obstacles. Frog jumps take off and land on two feet.
A.discovery: First lap: let children test each movement slowly and choose a comfortable way to do it; model eyes-forward, arms-out balance.
A.developing: Second lap: focus on one technique (stable feet, a soft bent-knee landing or steady balance). Give short feedback.
A.consolidating: Last lap: turn it into an imagined story mission while staying in control; children may choose a different safe route.
A.observation: Queues, fatigue, collisions and unstable or unsecured equipment.
A.review: 1. The board's course says 'time yourself, match it next lap' for the bear crawl. The Week 17 lesson says 'steady personal pace, no timed race', and the club rule bans speed contests, so the card has no timing. 2. The board's watch-for mentions a 'rope', but the course uses balance blocks, so the card says blocks. 3. The board has no set-up, learning cues or backup for this station. The set-up is from the lesson, and the cues are condensed from the lesson's laps and the course's how-to lines. 4. The soft mats come from the lesson checklist. 5. The board says 'count of 5 (both feet)' and the lesson says 'each side', so the card says each foot.

B.name: Challenge Trail
equipment: 10 cones (A–B markers and the one-way loop)
4 soft foam hurdles (they fall over if clipped)
B.setup: The same six stations as Week A. Week B: each child chooses one personal goal (a steady bear crawl, quiet two-foot landings or a five-count balance on each foot) and retests it on the last lap, without racing or comparing.
steps: Bear crawl — all fours from A to B, steady and controlled. No timing, no racing.
Frog jumps — TWO-foot jumps over the 4 flat markers; make every landing quiet.
Balance walk — the whole length of the low balance blocks: arms out, heel-to-toe, slow. You can also walk alongside them.
One-foot balance — look at one spot, arms out: a five-count on one foot, then the other.
Hurdle step-overs — lift your knees over the 4 soft foam hurdles; head up, keep moving.
Crab walk — backwards to the finish, hands behind, bottom up. On the last lap, retest your chosen goal.
B.younger: Low, wide pathways, supported balancing and fewer obstacles if needed.
B.older: Controlled arms-out balance and longer (but still manageable) challenges. Never raise the equipment.
B.watch: Frustration when they step off the blocks. Reassure them: 'stepping off is part of learning'. Also watch for queues, fatigue and collisions.
B.safety: Not a race: no timing, and children never compare their goals. Use soft foam hurdles that fall over if clipped, never rigid hurdles. Balance blocks stay on the ground, with no raised or unsecured obstacles. Frog jumps take off and land on two feet.
B.discovery: First lap: let children test each movement slowly and choose a comfortable way to do it; model eyes-forward, arms-out balance.
B.developing: Second lap: focus on one technique (stable feet, a soft bent-knee landing or steady balance) and choose a personal goal: a steady crawl, quiet two-foot landings or a five-count balance on each foot.
B.consolidating: Last lap: retest the chosen goal, staying in control and without racing or comparing children; children may choose a different safe route.
B.observation: Queues, fatigue, collisions and unstable or unsecured equipment.
B.review: 1. The Week B goal and retest come from the board's Week B progression and the Week 18 lesson's Week B focus. The board says 'five-count balance on both feet' and the lesson says 'on each foot', so the card says each foot. 2. The Week A issues apply here too: the board says 'time yourself' for the bear crawl (the card has no timing), and the board's watch-for says 'rope' (the card says blocks). 3. The board's learning cues are blank, so the cues are condensed from the Week B focus.
sources: Rotations board: S9 · R3 course and Week B progression

A.name: Long Jump — personal goal
equipment: 30 cones (take-off lines, waiting spaces, personal markers)
A.setup: An age-appropriate runway with a start line leading to the long jump mat or sandpit. Mark the waiting spaces and have a cone ready for each child's personal marker.
steps: Next to the line, swing your arms into a standing jump and land quietly.
Choose your take-off line. Swing and spring off TWO feet into the mat or pit.
Land on two feet with bent knees and freeze. Place your own cone where you landed.
Pick ONE thing to improve (arm swing, quiet landing or reach) and have three goes.
Try to beat your OWN cone. Nobody compares with anybody else.
A.younger: A supported standing jump.
A.older: An optional short approach, only with control. Take off from two feet and land on two feet.
A.watch: Children comparing themselves with each other. Redirect: 'beat your own cone'.
A.safety: Long jump = take off from two feet and land on two feet in the mat or pit, so no hopping here. Each child beats their OWN marker; never compare children. Wait in the marked waiting spaces.
A.discovery: Revisit the swing-arm standing jump and a quiet landing.
A.developing: Choose a take-off line, do a two-foot jump, freeze and mark your own landing.
A.consolidating: The child chooses one improvement target (arm swing OR quiet landing OR reach) for three attempts.
A.observation: No comparing distances between children.
A.alternative: Frog Jump Freeze: jump forward with two feet, then freeze the landing in a bent-knee shape.
A.review: 1. The board's set-up ('a start line and a long open run') and how-to ('jumps or hops from the line') come from the old Measure Your Hop game. The club long jump rule and the Week 17 lesson need a two-foot take-off and landing into the mat or pit, from a runway with waiting spaces, so the card says jump only and uses the lesson's set-up. Update the board. 2. The 5–6 short approach still ends in a two-foot take-off (club rule). Confirm. 3. On Thu 18 Mar the Run Jump Throw group has 'combination jumps', so check the pit or mat is free.

B.name: Long Jump — celebration
equipment: 30 cones (take-off lines, waiting spaces, personal markers)
B.setup: The same runway and mat or sandpit as Week A, with marked waiting spaces and a personal marker cone for each child. Short, controlled run-ups only, and only for ready 5–6-year-olds.
steps: Explore a standing jump with your arms helping.
Use the same start every time: push off two feet, reach, and land quietly on two feet in the mat or pit. Stay balanced.
Place your own cone. Compare only with your own earlier jumps.
Everyone has one final personal challenge.
Celebrate each child's technique or confidence, not just the distance. Nobody compares with anybody else.
B.younger: A shorter line and a personal success marker.
B.older: A short, controlled run-up, then a two-foot take-off and a coordinated two-foot landing.
B.watch: Unsafe jumping for distance: stop it straight away. Also children comparing themselves with each other. Redirect: 'beat your own cone'.
B.safety: Long jump = take off from two feet and land on two feet in the mat or pit. Each child compares only with their OWN earlier jumps, never with other children. Short, controlled run-ups only. Wait in the marked waiting spaces.
B.discovery: Explore a standing jump with the arms helping.
B.developing: Rehearse the same start and landing; compare with your own earlier attempts.
B.consolidating: One final personal challenge; celebrate technique or confidence rather than measurement alone.
B.observation: Stop any unsafe jumping for distance.
B.alternative: Frog Jump Freeze: jump forward with two feet, then freeze the landing in a bent-knee shape.
B.review: 1. The board's set-up and how-to are written for Week A, so these Week B steps come from the board's Week B progression and the Week 18 lesson. 2. The 5–6 'short controlled run-up' is written as ending in a two-foot take-off, to match the club long jump rule. Confirm. 3. Thu 25 Mar has nothing on the senior schedule, so the pit or mat should be free.

meet.title: Week 19 — Mini Meet, skill passport and prizegiving
meet.coachNote: This is a festival, not formal testing, ranking or competition. Four colour teams rotate through four zones every 8 minutes. At each zone children explore, practise, then choose an optional challenge, and the helper marks participation, not mastery. Each zone needs at least one responsible helper, plus a roaming safety lead. Every child is named, gets a certificate and hears one personalised observation (one movement or social achievement since October). Nobody leaves without their name being called.

runOfShow.label: Welcome and passports
runOfShow.detail: Children pick a colour team. Walk the boundaries, explain the four friendly zones and show the passport stickers or stamps. Parents watch from outside the movement lanes.

runOfShow.label: Zones — rotation 1
runOfShow.detail: Each colour team starts at a different zone. Children explore, then practise, then choose an optional challenge. The helper marks participation, not mastery, with a sticker.

runOfShow.label: Zones — rotation 2
runOfShow.detail: Teams move on to the next zone. Every zone runs at the same time.

runOfShow.label: Zones — rotation 3
runOfShow.detail: Teams move on to the next zone.

runOfShow.label: Zones — rotation 4
runOfShow.detail: Last zone. Every team has now visited all four zones and has four stickers.

runOfShow.label: Friendly sprint finish
runOfShow.detail: One age-appropriate run each, through run-through markers: 3–4 years 15 m, 5 years 20 m, 6 years 25–30 m. Run THROUGH the finish, not up to it. Every child is announced. No timing and no placings. It is a celebration run, not a race.

runOfShow.label: Certificates and prizegiving
runOfShow.detail: Every child is named, receives a certificate and hears one personalised observation. Use a microphone if one is available. A short group photo only with guardian consent. Finish with an optional gentle parachute circle. Nobody leaves without their name being called.

zones.name: Run and Dodge
equipment: Cones for a travel route and wide gates
zones.setup: A roomy coned area with a cone route and wide gates, clear of the throwing and striking lanes. Mark walking lanes with wider gaps for the youngest.
steps: Explore: travel along the cones at a comfortable speed, eyes up.
Practise: pump your arms. On the call, bend and plant, then go a new way.
Challenge (optional): friendly Traffic Lights. GREEN = jog, ORANGE = walk, RED = freeze.
Then a low-speed chase and dodge through the wide gates. Nobody is out.
Sticker: every child who has a go gets the Run and Dodge sticker. It is for taking part, not for being fastest.
zones.watch: Children watching the floor instead of the space, and collisions. Keep the gates wide and the chase slow.
zones.safety: Low-speed chase with gentle tags only. No elimination and no races. Running stays clear of the throwing and striking lanes.
zones.discovery: Travel along cones at a comfortable speed, eyes up.
zones.developing: Pump arms. Bend and plant before choosing a new direction on a verbal signal.
zones.consolidating: Friendly Traffic Lights, then a low-speed chase and dodge through wide gates (no elimination).
zones.observation: Are eyes looking ahead, and are children avoiding collisions? Mark participation, not mastery.
zones.review: The Week 19 page lists equipment for the whole night with no quantities, so no cone count is given here (Traffic Lights normally uses 20 cones on Rotations board S1 · R1). The page has no watch-for for this zone, so the watch and observation lines and the GREEN/ORANGE/RED calls come from the Traffic Lights row on the Rotations board.
sources: Rotations board: S1 · R1 (Traffic Lights calls, watch-for, observation)

zones.name: Hop, Skip, Jump and Balance
equipment: Long jump pit or landing mat (club rule — standing long jump)
zones.setup: A ground-level course of flat hoops and markers with small mini-challenges. Nothing is raised or fixed. Put the standing long jump at the edge of the pit or mat.
steps: Explore: stand on one foot, march with a step-hop, then do a two-foot jump to a flat marker.
Practise hopping: the same foot takes off and lands.
Practise skipping (step-hop, alternating feet), a standing long jump with an arm swing into the pit or mat (two feet take off, two feet land) and a 3-count flamingo balance.
Challenge (optional): pick two mini-challenges around the hoop and marker course. Finish with a quiet two-foot landing.
Sticker: every child who has a go gets the zone sticker. It is for trying, not for how far or how long.
zones.younger: Hand support and very small movements.
zones.older: Choose two mini-challenges from the course and finish with a quiet two-foot landing.
zones.watch: Hops that land on the other foot, when the same foot should take off and land. Loud, stiff landings: cue 'land quietly'.
zones.safety: Ground-level hoops and markers only, with no raised or fixed obstacles. Hopping: take off and land on the SAME foot. Jumping: take off and land on two feet. Standing long jump: two feet take off and land in the pit or on the mat. No measuring, and never compare children's jumps.
zones.discovery: Stand on one foot, march a step-hop, and do a two-foot jump at a flat marker.
zones.developing: Hop on the same take-off and landing foot. Skip with an alternating step-hop. Swing the arms in a standing long jump into the pit or mat. Hold a 3-count flamingo.
zones.consolidating: Pick two mini-challenges through a ground-level hoop and marker course. Finish with a quiet two-foot landing.
zones.observation: Mark participation, not mastery. Note anything useful for the certificates, for example trying both feet in a balance.
zones.review: The page gives no separate 5–6 option for this zone, so the older line uses the zone's optional challenge. The page doesn't name a landing surface for the standing long jump. The card follows the club rule (into the pit or mat). Please confirm this zone can run beside the pit. No equipment quantities are given. The page has no watch-for, so the watch line is condensed from the zone's cues.

zones.name: Throw, Push and Catch
zones.skill: Underarm and overarm throwing · chest push · catching
equipment: Cones or flat markers for the one-way throwing zone
zones.setup: Small stations that all face safe, dedicated target zones, throwing one way and away from the running and striking areas. The stations are hoop toss, a one-way distance zone, a chest pass to a ready adult and a soft-catch spot.
steps: Explore: roll a beanbag, catch a scarf, and try a gentle two-handed chest push.
Practise: an underarm pendulum throw to a hoop, then an overarm side-on throw, stepping with the opposite foot.
Practise catching a soft object with the elbows bending.
Challenge (optional): pick two stations: hoop toss (underarm), the one-way distance zone (overarm), a chest pass to a ready adult, or a soft catch with one bounce.
Retrieve only on the helper's signal. Every child who has a go gets the zone sticker.
zones.younger: Large soft balls, an adult feeding them, and a short distance.
zones.older: Choose two of the challenge stations.
zones.watch: Throws that don't face the target zone, and children retrieving before the signal.
zones.safety: Soft equipment only: beanbags, scarves and soft balls. Every throw goes one way into its dedicated target zone, away from the running paths and the striking lane. Retrieve only on the signal, and never across another lane. No measuring and no comparing children's throws.
zones.discovery: Roll a beanbag and catch a scarf. Try a gentle two-handed chest push.
zones.developing: Underarm pendulum throw to a hoop. Overarm side-on throw with an opposite step. Receive a soft object with the elbows bending.
zones.consolidating: Pick two stations: hoop toss (underarm), one-way distance zone (overarm), chest pass to a ready adult, or soft catch with one bounce.
zones.observation: Mark participation, not mastery. Note anything useful for the certificates, for example moving into a catch.
zones.review: The page gives no separate 5–6 option for this zone, so the older line uses the zone's optional challenge. The materials list says 'scarf/balloons', but the zone only uses scarves, so the card lists scarves. No quantities or watch-for are given. The watch line comes from the page's target-zone rule and the club's retrieval rule.

zones.name: Kick, Strike and Relay
zones.skill: Kicking · striking off a tee · relay handover
equipment: Cones for a two-cone dribble route and a wide goal
Net for the striking target area (not on the page's materials list)
zones.setup: Three physically separate lanes: a dribble-and-kick lane with a wide goal, a foam-bat tee lane hitting one way into a netted target area, and a short walking relay lane.
steps: Explore: short taps on a still soft football, touch the ball on the tee with the foam bat, and hand a beanbag over.
Practise: plant the non-kicking foot beside the ball and swing through. Stand side-on for a two-handed swing. Face your partner for the handover.
Challenge (optional): dribble through two cones and kick at the wide goal, then do a foam-bat tee hit into the netted area.
Finish with a gentle walking relay. Place the beanbag in your partner's hand and never throw it.
Every child who has a go gets the zone sticker.
zones.younger: Adult assistants, wide gates, stationary balls and a soft bat.
zones.older: The full challenge: dribble through two cones and kick at the goal, do the tee hit, then the walking relay.
zones.watch: Children drifting into the swing lane, kicks or hits while someone is retrieving, and thrown handovers.
zones.safety: Foam bats and soft balls only. The swing lane is physically separated from kicking, throwing and running. Hit one way into the net, and retrieve only on the signal. Relay: hand the beanbag over hand to hand. Never throw it, and no blind handovers. An adult supervises every handover.
zones.discovery: Short taps on a still soft football. Touch a stationary tee ball with a foam bat. Hand a beanbag over.
zones.developing: Plant the non-kicking foot beside the ball and swing through. Stand side-on for a two-handed swing. Face your partner for the transfer.
zones.consolidating: Dribble through two cones and kick at a wide goal. Do a foam-bat tee hit into a netted target area, then a gentle walking relay handover.
zones.observation: Mark participation, not mastery. Note anything useful for the certificates, for example encouraging a teammate.
zones.review: The netted target area for the tee hit isn't on the page's materials list, so please confirm a net is available. The page gives no separate 5–6 option, so the older line uses the zone's challenge. No quantities or watch-for are given. The watch line comes from the page's separated swing lanes and the club's relay and retrieval rules.
